observations.expected: Flowing thick anterior ossification bridges at least four contiguous vertebral bodies.
observations.observed: There is clearly visible flowing, undulating anterior ossification along the thoracic and upper lumbar spine, bridging multiple contiguous vertebral bodies (well more than four), with the characteristic 'melted candle wax' appearance of DISH along the anterior and right lateral vertebral margins.

observations.expected: Disc heights are relatively preserved; severe disc collapse does not dominate the pattern.
observations.observed: Intervertebral disc spaces are visible and reasonably maintained throughout the thoracic spine. There is no severe disc collapse or dominant disc space narrowing; the disc heights appear relatively preserved consistent with DISH rather than degenerative disc disease.

observations.expected: The visible vertebral bodies and posterior elements are anatomically coherent.
observations.observed: The vertebral column forms a single continuous chain with no duplication, floating vertebrae, or garbled segments. Vertebral bodies are sequentially sized and stacked. Posterior elements including spinous processes are visible and coherent. No AI artifact duplication or impossible anatomy is identified.
